name: Aglaonema
summary: Also known as: Chinese evergreen. Low-light tolerant aroids with variegated foliage in shades of green, silver, pink, or red.
description:
Also known as: Chinese evergreen. Low-light tolerant aroids with variegated foliage in shades of green, silver, pink, or red.

Examples: Aglaonema commutatum (Chinese evergreen), A. pictum, A. 'Silver Bay', A. 'Maria', A. 'Red Siam', A. 'Pink Star'

Origin: Tropical Asia

Care guidance: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil feels dry. Keep slightly more moist than other low-light plants but avoid soggy soil. Bright indirect light maintains variegation; low light is tolerated but may reduce color. Maintain 50-60% humidity. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced liquid fertilizer (20-20-20) diluted to half strength. Wipe leaves monthly with damp cloth to remove dust and improve photosynthesis. Repot every 2-3 years in spring when roots fill container. Prune yellowing leaves at base. Watch for spider mites in dry conditions. Toxic to pets.

description:

Care guidance: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil is dry. Keep moderately moist but never soggy—prone to root rot. Bright indirect light preferred; tolerates light shade. Prune yellowing or damaged leaves at the base. Trim leggy growth to maintain shape.

name: Cast Iron Plant
summary: Also known as: Barroom plant. Extremely low-light tolerant foliage plant in the Asparagaceae family, named for its ability to survive neglect. Includes various cultivars like variegated and speckled varieties.
description:
Also known as: Barroom plant. Extremely low-light tolerant foliage plant in the Asparagaceae family, named for its ability to survive neglect. Includes various cultivars like variegated and speckled varieties.

Examples: Aspidistra elatior (Cast iron plant, Barroom plant), A. elatior 'Variegata' (Variegated cast iron plant), A. elatior 'Milky Way' (speckled variety)

Origin: China

Care guidance: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil is dry. Extremely forgiving of inconsistent watering and low light conditions. Avoid overwatering which causes root rot. Tolerates very low light but grows faster in bright indirect light. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year during growing season with balanced fertilizer at quarter strength. Repot only when severely root-bound (every 5-7 years). Remove dead or yellowing leaves at base by cutting at soil level. Dust leaves occasionally. One of the most indestructible houseplants. Prune yellowing or damaged leaves at the base. Trim leggy growth to maintain shape.

Prune brown tips and remove yellowing lower leaves. Sensitive to drafts and temperature fluctuations. Toxic to pets.

name: Dracaena Goldieana
summary: Also known as: Zebra-striped dragon tree. Rare dracaena with striking horizontal zebra-like bands of dark and light green on broad, oval leaves. A trending collector plant.
description:
Also known as: Zebra-striped dragon tree. Rare dracaena with striking horizontal zebra-like bands of dark and light green on broad, oval leaves. A trending collector plant.

Examples: Dracaena goldieana (Zebra-striped dragon tree, Queen of dracaenas)

Origin: West Africa

Care guidance: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil are dry; more sensitive to overwatering than other dracaenas. Bright indirect light — more light than typical dracaenas to maintain bold banding. High humidity (60%+) preferred — this is the key to success; brown leaf edges indicate low humidity. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Grows slowly. More finicky than other dracaenas — treat more like a calathea in terms of humidity needs. Repot every 2-3 years. Toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or damaged leaves promptly.

name: Snake Plant
summary: Also known as: Mother-in-law's tongue. Extremely low-maintenance succulents in the Asparagaceae family with upright sword-like leaves. Includes various cultivars with different leaf shapes and patterns.
description:
Also known as: Mother-in-law's tongue. Extremely low-maintenance succulents in the Asparagaceae family with upright sword-like leaves. Includes various cultivars with different leaf shapes and patterns.

Examples: Dracaena trifasciata (syn. Sansevieria trifasciata; Mother-in-law's tongue), D. trifasciata 'Laurentii', D. trifasciata 'Moonshine', D. trifasciata 'Black Gold', Dracaena angolensis (syn. Sansevieria cylindrica; cylindrical snake plant)

Origin: West Africa

Care guidance: Water only when soil is completely dry (every 2-8 weeks depending on conditions). Very drought tolerant due to water storage in leaves. Bright indirect to direct light preferred; tolerates low light but grows slowly. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year during growing season with succulent fertilizer at quarter strength. Repot only when pot breaks or plant becomes top-heavy (every 5-10 years). Remove dead leaves at base by pulling gently. Divide offsets when repotting. Overwatering is the main cause of death - when in doubt, wait longer. Toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or damaged leaves promptly.

name: Spider Plants
summary: Also known as: Airplane plant, Ribbon plant. Easy-care trailing plants in the Asparagaceae family that produce plantlets on stolons, excellent air purifiers. Includes various cultivars with different variegation patterns.
description:
Also known as: Airplane plant, Ribbon plant. Easy-care trailing plants in the Asparagaceae family that produce plantlets on stolons, excellent air purifiers. Includes various cultivars with different variegation patterns.

Examples: Chlorophytum comosum (Spider plant, Airplane plant, Ribbon plant), C. comosum 'Vittatum', C. comosum 'Variegatum', C. comosum 'Bonnie'

Origin: Southern Africa

Care guidance: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Keep slightly moist but avoid overwatering which causes brown tips. Bright indirect light maintains variegation. Medium humidity (40-50%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength. Remove plantlets when they develop roots (2-3 inches long) to propagate or reduce crowding. Trim brown tips with clean scissors. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Excellent air purifier. Watch for spider mites in dry conditions. Non-toxic to pets.

name: ZZ Plant
summary: Also known as: Zanzibar gem, Eternity plant. Extremely low-maintenance plant in the Araceae family with glossy leaves and rhizomes that store water, virtually indestructible.
description:

Examples: Zamioculcas zamiifolia (ZZ plant, Zanzibar gem, Eternity plant), Z. zamiifolia 'Raven' (Raven ZZ)

Care guidance: Water when soil is completely dry (every 2-4 weeks). Rhizomes store water making it extremely drought tolerant. Overwatering causes root rot - when in doubt, wait. Repot every 2-3 years when rhizomes fill container. Wipe glossy leaves monthly to remove dust. Virtually indestructible - perfect for beginners. Toxic to pets. Remove old, yellowing, or diseased leaves promptly.

name: Palms
summary: Tropical and subtropical plants in the Arecaceae family with architectural fronds, popular for adding a tropical feel indoors and outdoors.
description:
Tropical and subtropical plants in the Arecaceae family with architectural fronds, popular for adding a tropical feel indoors and outdoors.

Examples: Chamaedorea elegans (Parlor palm), Dypsis lutescens (Areca palm, Butterfly palm), Howea forsteriana (Kentia palm), Rhapis excelsa (Lady palm)

Origin: Tropics worldwide

Care guidance: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Do not overwater — root rot is the most common cause of palm death. Bright indirect light preferred; most tolerate lower light. Medium to high humidity (40-60%) preferred — mist regularly or use a humidifier. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with palm-specific fertilizer. Do not cut brown tips — trim just above the brown line. Remove only fully brown fronds. Repot infrequently — palms dislike root disturbance. Watch for spider mites and mealybugs.

name: Lithops
summary: Stone-like succulents that mimic pebbles in their native habitat, have specific dormancy periods when they should not be watered.
description:
Stone-like succulents that mimic pebbles in their native habitat, have specific dormancy periods when they should not be watered.

Examples: Lithops (Living stones, Pebble plants), various species with different colors and patterns

Origin: Southern Africa

Care guidance: Water sparingly in fall when new leaves emerge. Keep dry in summer dormancy and during winter/spring splitting. Very minimal watering even when active (every 2-4 weeks); water from below and let the pot drain fully. Bright direct light essential. Low humidity preferred. Fertilize very sparingly during active growth only. Repot every 3-5 years in very well-draining soil. Stone-like appearance mimics pebbles. Very specific care requirements. Leave the old leaf pair in place until it is completely papery, then remove it.

name: Christmas Cactus
summary: Also known as: True Christmas cactus. Forest cactus that blooms around Christmas, requires cool temperatures and reduced light to flower, has rounded leaf segments.
description:
Also known as: True Christmas cactus. Forest cactus that blooms around Christmas, requires cool temperatures and reduced light to flower, has rounded leaf segments.

Examples: Schlumbergera × buckleyi (Christmas cactus, True Christmas cactus), S. truncata (Thanksgiving cactus, Crab cactus)

Origin: Brazil

Care guidance: Keep soil slightly moist spring through summer. Reduce watering in fall (September-October) to encourage blooms - this triggers bud formation. More frequent watering than desert cacti. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct hot sun. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Cool temperatures (15-18°C) and reduced light in fall encourage flowering. Repot every 2-3 years. Rounded leaf segments distinguish from Thanksgiving cactus. Remove any dead or damaged pads or segments with clean, sharp tools. Minimal pruning needed.

name: Cymbidium
summary: Also known as: Boat orchid. Terrestrial and semi-terrestrial orchids in the Orchidaceae family with grassy leaves and tall sprays of long-lasting waxy flowers in winter and spring; the big hybrids are florist staples, while the small Chinese species have been cultivated for their fragrance for over two thousand years.
description:
Also known as: Boat orchid. Terrestrial and semi-terrestrial orchids in the Orchidaceae family with grassy leaves and tall sprays of long-lasting waxy flowers in winter and spring; the big hybrids are florist staples, while the small Chinese species have been cultivated for their fragrance for over two thousand years.

Examples: Cymbidium hybrids (Standard cymbidium), miniature cymbidiums, C. goeringii (Chinese spring orchid, Chunlan), C. ensifolium (Jianlan, Four-season orchid), C. sinense (Moxian), C. kanran (Hanlan)

Origin: Himalayas, East Asia, and Southeast Asia

Care guidance: Water thoroughly when the top of the mix dries, roughly weekly in summer and every 10-14 days in winter; the pseudobulbs should never shrivel. Bright light, more than most orchids, with light shade from midday summer sun; leaves should be yellow-green, not dark green. Grow at 10-27°C, and give a drop to 10-14°C on autumn nights to set flower spikes; standard hybrids will not bloom in constantly warm rooms. Medium humidity (40-60%). Feed every 2 weeks spring to summer with a balanced orchid fertilizer, switching to a low-nitrogen formula in late summer. Pot in a coarse bark mix in a snug pot; repot every 2-3 years after flowering. Spend summer outdoors in dappled shade if possible. Non-toxic to pets. Cut spent flower spikes at the base and remove dead leaf sheaths; divide crowded clumps leaving 3-4 bulbs per division.

Also known as: Lady's slipper orchid. Terrestrial orchids prized for their distinctive pouch-shaped lip that traps pollinating insects, with blooms in rich earth tones, greens, and dramatic spotted or striped patterns.

Care guidance: Keep potting mix evenly moist but never soggy; water when top layer feels slightly dry. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description:
Also known as: Moth orchid. Moth orchids, most common and beginner-friendly orchid genus in the Orchidaceae family with long-lasting blooms. Available in various colors.

Examples: Phalaenopsis (Moth orchid, Phal), various hybrid cultivars in many colors

Origin: Southeast Asia

Care guidance: Soak roots weekly for 15-20 minutes, then allow to dry between waterings. Never let sit in water. Avoid getting water in crown (center) which causes fatal crown rot. Use well-draining orchid bark mix, never regular potting soil. Bright indirect light preferred; direct sun burns leaves. High humidity (50-70%) preferred. Fertilize weekly spring through fall with orchid fertilizer at quarter strength. Repot every 1-2 years when bark breaks down. Blooms last 2-3 months. Most beginner-friendly orchid. After blooming, cut the spent spike above a node to encourage a secondary spike, or at the base once it browns.

summary: Also known as: Christmas star, Mexican flame leaf. Winter-flowering shrub in the Euphorbiaceae family whose showy red, pink, white, or marbled bracts surround tiny yellow flowers; the classic holiday houseplant.
description:
Also known as: Christmas star, Mexican flame leaf. Winter-flowering shrub in the Euphorbiaceae family whose showy red, pink, white, or marbled bracts surround tiny yellow flowers; the classic holiday houseplant.

Examples: Euphorbia pulcherrima (Poinsettia, Christmas star), 'Prestige Red', 'Winter Rose' (curled bracts), 'Ice Punch', 'Princettia' (compact pink)

Origin: Mexico

Care guidance: Water when the top inch of soil is dry; never let the pot sit in water or in a sealed foil sleeve. Bright indirect light for at least 6 hours a day. Keep at 18-24°C and away from cold drafts, radiators, and windowpanes; chilling below 10°C drops leaves. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly at half strength only while in active growth; stop while bracts are colored. Bracts color only after 14 hours of total darkness nightly for 8-10 weeks from early autumn. Cut stems back to 10-15 cm in spring to rebloom. Mildly toxic to pets; may cause GI upset, and the milky sap can irritate skin. Prune leggy stems in spring and pinch tips in summer for a bushy plant.

name: Baby's Tears
summary: Also known as: Mind-your-own-business, Angel's tears. Creeping Mediterranean perennial in the Urticaceae family that forms a dense, bright-green carpet of tiny round leaves; grown as a terrarium and pot-topping houseplant and as a shade groundcover in mild climates.
description:
Also known as: Mind-your-own-business, Angel's tears. Creeping Mediterranean perennial in the Urticaceae family that forms a dense, bright-green carpet of tiny round leaves; grown as a terrarium and pot-topping houseplant and as a shade groundcover in mild climates.

Examples: Soleirolia soleirolii (Baby's tears), 'Aurea' (golden), 'Variegata' (silver-edged)

Origin: Corsica and Sardinia

Care guidance: Keep the soil consistently moist but never soggy; it wilts dramatically when dry and usually recovers after watering. Water from below or at the soil line; wet foliage left in the dark can rot. Bright indirect light; direct sun scorches it. Comfortable at 10-24°C; frost kills the top growth outdoors. High humidity (50%+) keeps it lush, which is why it thrives in terrariums. Feed monthly in spring and summer at half strength. Perennial outdoors in zones 9-11, where it can become invasive. Non-toxic to pets. Trim with scissors any time to keep the mat tidy and to stop it smothering neighbors.

name: Purple Passion Plant
summary: Also known as: Velvet plant, Purple velvet plant, Gynura. Trailing houseplant in the Asteraceae family whose green leaves are covered in iridescent purple hairs that glow in bright light; the small orange flowers smell unpleasant and are usually pinched off.
description:
Also known as: Velvet plant, Purple velvet plant, Gynura. Trailing houseplant in the Asteraceae family whose green leaves are covered in iridescent purple hairs that glow in bright light; the small orange flowers smell unpleasant and are usually pinched off.

Examples: Gynura aurantiaca (Purple passion plant, Velvet plant), 'Purple Passion' (compact trailing form), G. sarmentosa (trailing velvet plant)

Origin: Java

Care guidance: Water when the top 2-3 cm of soil is dry; keep slightly moist but never soggy, and water the soil rather than the fuzzy leaves, which spot and rot when wet. Bright indirect light keeps the purple intense; direct sun scorches and low light turns it green. Comfortable at 16-27°C; keep above 13°C. Medium humidity (40-60%). Feed every 2-4 weeks in spring and summer at half strength. Well-draining, peat-based potting mix. Aphids and spider mites hide in the hairs, so inspect often. Short-lived; take cuttings every year or two to replace leggy plants. Non-toxic to pets. Pinch stem tips regularly to keep it bushy and remove the malodorous flower buds as they form.

Stems root wherever they touch soil and cuttings root in a glass of water within a week. Perennial outdoors only in zones 10-11; grown in hanging baskets elsewhere. Non-toxic to pets. Pinch stem tips often to prevent legginess and cut back hard in spring if it becomes sparse.

description:
Colorful foliage plants in the Acanthaceae family with spotted leaves in pink, red, or white, pinch to maintain bushy growth.

Examples: Hypoestes phyllostachya (Polka dot plant, Freckle face), various color cultivars

Origin: Madagascar

Care guidance: Keep soil evenly moist, avoid letting dry out. High humidity (60%+) preferred - use humidifier or pebble tray. Bright indirect light maintains vibrant colors. Fertilize every 2 weeks spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Pinch tips regularly to encourage branching and maintain bushy growth. Pinch flowers immediately to prolong plant life. Repot annually. Annual in most climates. Easy to propagate from cuttings.
